title: Low-overhead evidence capture
statement: Splitstick must add no more than 1 ms per event at p95 and 3 ms per event at p99 on a defined reference environment, measured over at least one million representative events across multiple benchmark runs. Measurements must include content commitment, encryption and local persistence, exclude deferred checkpoint and witness operations, and report sustained throughput and memory behaviour. The engineering stretch target remains p99 below 1 ms. Durability and integrity are never traded for latency: no deferring a critical write without guaranteed recovery, no weakening source-sequence or failure reporting, no removing encryption or commitment checks, and no uncontrolled buffering to improve a benchmark.
source: Numbers we are signing up to
verify: Benchmark harness on the reference environment defined in bench/reference-env.json: p95 and p99 over at least 1e6 events, at least three repeats, reporting p50/p95/p99/p99.9, throughput, memory and GC activity. The harness declares each run an acceptance measurement or a regression metric and names every shortfall, and it verifies its own instruments — clock resolution and the GC recorder — in the same run. A run that meets p95 but not the p99 stretch target is a pass against the budget and is reported as such.
note: M1 status: open pending a qualifying run. Measured on the development machine (a regression metric, not acceptance): p50 0.23 ms, p95 0.49 ms, p99 1.77 ms against p95<=1 ms and p99<=3 ms. GC measured at 71 pauses coinciding with 56% of the slowest 1% of samples; filesystem latency accounts for much of the rest. Two earlier attributions here were withdrawn — one asserted without measurement, one on a measurement whose instrument was never validated. Closing it is tracked in docs/m1-follow-ups.md, including the limits of the qualification check: cpus, memory and load cannot establish that a machine is dedicated or that its storage is comparable, so an acceptance run must also name its machine and storage. M7 follow-up: an attempt to take a qualifying measurement found the qualification check could not be satisfied on any host. max_load_average_1m was evaluated against a load average sampled AFTER the measured loop, and one saturated single-threaded process raises its own one-minute average to roughly 1.0 against a limit of 1.0 — the constraint whose stated purpose is to exclude a machine under other load was scoring this benchmark's load. Two of the three exclusions the reference file lists in prose (a shared CI runner, a filesystem near capacity) had no evaluator at all, while the file asserted every constraint in it was evaluated. Both are fixed: pre-run constraints read a host sample taken before any measured work, qualifyRun throws rather than falling back to the post-run reading, and forbid_ci and min_free_disk_gb now exist. The unit tests missed this because they handed qualifyRun a hand-built observation — the guard was tested and the call site was not — so a test now asserts the sampling order in both benchmark sources and fails loudly when it cannot find its anchor. This does not close NFR-01; it makes closing it possible.

title: Run latency budget
statement: Added end-to-end agent run latency below 2%.
source: Numbers we are signing up to
verify: Interleaved A/B through the real OMA orchestrator, analysed as a paired difference because the arms alternate run by run. The verdict requires the whole 95% interval to sit below the budget; a budget falling inside the interval is reported as UNRESOLVED rather than as a pass. The harness records its environment and checks its clock resolution.
evidence: bench/run-latency.mjs — 40 paired runs: added 0.864 ms, 95% interval [-1.612, 3.340] ms, entirely below the 16.975 ms the 2% budget allows, so the budget is established rather than merely not contradicted. Instruments self-checked in the same run.

title: Verification throughput
statement: Verify a 100,000-event run in under 2 seconds, offline.
source: Numbers we are signing up to
verify: Benchmark on a documented reference machine
evidence: bench/verify.mjs measures total elapsed against the 2 s budget on the WORST run, not a percentile and not the median: an auditor runs it once and 'usually under two seconds' is not the claim. STATUS: NOT MET, and not for want of a reference host. With the O(checkpoints x n) consistency- proof regeneration fixed (prefixRoots plus a locally-confirmed-root set, which took the same measurement from 76,005 ms to 15,849 ms), verifying 100,000 records measures 15,849 ms median and 24,145 ms worst against a 2,000 ms budget — about 8x over. 1,235 ms of that is the floor the filesystem and JSON.parse impose on reading the journals at all, so 62% of the budget is spent before any verification happens, and JCS canonicalisation at ~19 microseconds a record is a further ~1.9 s on its own. A gap of that shape does not close on faster hardware: it closes either through substantial further work on the verify path (a JCS fast path; making content reproduction opt-in, since chain and inclusion verification do not need every plaintext) or through a deliberately revised budget with a measurement behind it, which is the precedent M1 set for NFR-01's own budget. Separately, every NFR-04 run used to report '100000 events < 1000000' because it was evaluated against NFR-01's reference block; the two now have their own constraints, so an NFR-04 run can state a real shortfall instead of a borrowed one.

title: HSM/KMS support
statement: Operate with a KMS or HSM offering non-exportable keys.
source: Getting started — a KMS or HSM
verify: Integration test against at least one KMS and one HSM. The KMS half runs via npm run test:kms against a real ECC_NIST_EDWARDS25519 key and asserts the signature verifies under an independent Ed25519 implementation, not only under ours; it reports NOT VERIFIED and skips when no key is configured, so a green suite never reads as having verified it.
note: M2 status: open. The KMS adapter is built and its failure paths are covered against a fake, but the interoperability test needs a real AWS key and has not run. The HSM half is blocked: of the products that sign Ed25519, AWS KMS issues no per-key attestation and GCP offers Ed25519 at software protection level only, so independently-supported custody needs hardware — and the YubiHSM 2 purchase is on hold until its attestation capability is confirmed. See docs/kms-capability-matrix.md.

title: MCP transport coverage
statement: Support MCP over stdio and HTTP.
verify: E2E per transport
evidence: Both transports, and a test asserts they produce the SAME record field for field — not down to the commitments, because a content cid is salted per store and comparing cids across stores compares two random salts. The equivalence that matters is the shape and the plaintext, and both are asserted. DES-14 makes the format adapter-independent so a verifier never needs to know which transport wrote a pack

title: Never degrade availability
statement: The collector must never be able to stop or block an agent run.
source: Operations — no audit layer that can take down production
verify: Absolute: a whole run completes with every witness unreachable, and no configuration can make the collector block
evidence: packages/core/test/queue.test.mjs; SCOPE-16's on_unavailable admits one value and there is no fail-closed setting to choose

title: Durable local queue
statement: Unwitnessed batches survive process restart and are re-submitted.
verify: The queue is a journal, read from disk on open; a drain is durable across restart; a torn tail is dropped AND repaired before the next append; damage in the middle is refused rather than skipped
evidence: Store.appendQueue/writeQueue/readQueue; an in-memory queue lost exactly the evidence an outage created, and an outage is when a restart is most likely. The append fast path then persisted the WRONG entry: the queue is kept ordered by checkpoint_seq, so an out-of-order enqueue landed mid-array while the append wrote the new entry at the end, leaving a disk order that no restart could reconcile with memory. A damaged entry is refused on read rather than coerced, because a queue that silently drops the unreadable loses the submission it was holding

title: Resist collector stoppage
statement: Stopping the collector and claiming a quiet period must be detectable, by heartbeat discontinuity. Patching the collector is NOT covered: a modified build can report the original digest, and a self-reported digest is not remote attestation.
verify: Kill the collector mid-window; the coverage report shows an undeclared gap. A separate test asserts a collector reporting a forged digest is NOT flagged, so the limit is pinned by a test rather than by prose
evidence: Heartbeat discontinuity as COVERAGE_GAP (red-team G, detected) and the patched collector as a declared limit (red-team G2, undetected by construction — a patched collector never allocates the number, so there is nothing to remove). G2 first removed the action from an honest store and was DETECTED via the source_seq hole, which would have credited AC-6 for catching something it does not catch The coverage report refuses a completeness claim when no heartbeat falls in the window, because the mechanism being absent is not the mechanism reporting continuity.

title: Resist policy downgrade
statement: Weakening the anchoring policy before tampering must be visible in the record.
verify: Test weakens the witness set, then asserts a countersigned policy event appears in the chain before the next batch
evidence: policy.mjs + Store.writePolicyDocument/readPolicyDocument; red-team H (tamper after a recorded downgrade, LEAF_MISMATCH) and H2 (delete the policy record, SEQ_BROKEN + CHAIN_BROKEN). DES-09 specified two digests and called the result a record of the weakening; two opaque digests make the change detectable without making its DIRECTION identifiable, so the document the chain commits to is stored and a substituted one is not returned

title: Erasure via crypto-shredding
statement: Support a documented erasure procedure satisfying a data-subject deletion request, over payloads, content salts, leaf salts, the reference index, the agent label and any approval reviewer. The claim is scoped to that enumerated set, not to all personal information everywhere.
verify: Procedure executed; the enumerated set is unrecoverable; an independent privacy assessment of the residue is deferred to a funded release and recorded as such
evidence: residue.mjs scanResidue over the five erasable payloads — the agent label, both payloads, the approval reviewer and the reviewed request — each asserted unretrievable afterwards, with an unrelated record's payloads untouched. The independent privacy assessment of the residue remains deferred to a funded release, as the requirement says

title: Chain survives erasure
statement: The chain still verifies after content deletion.
verify: Verify passes post-deletion
evidence: verifyStore after shredRecord: failed is 0, and every finding is inconclusive — CONTENT_ABSENT and LEAF_INCONCLUSIVE — never fail

title: Minimal retained artefacts
statement: After erasure the chain retains only the version-1 permanent set: v, collector, run, record_seq, source_seq, ts, kind, consequential, tool, outcome, attempt, correlation, approval.decision, result.ok, args.bytes, result.bytes, a padding record pad nonce, gap spans, unknown-loss intervals, and salted digests, leaf digests and chain heads. Every other field is erasable: payloads, the agent label, the approval reviewer, the reviewed request, content salts, leaf salts and the reference index. The byte lengths and the correlation relationship are documented residual leaks with no mitigation in 1.0.
source: Erasure — what survives is a salted hash and a timestamp
verify: Automated scan after crypto-shredding asserts the residue matches the enumerated permanent set exactly, field for field, across every record kind including padding; the list is derived from the version-1 schema so a schema change fails the test rather than silently passing
evidence: residue.mjs CLASSIFIED + classifySchema + scanResidue, with four codes in the shared vocabulary. The classification is checked against ALLOWED so extending the record format fails the scan rather than letting a new field survive a deletion request by default; classifySchema takes the schema as a parameter so a test can prove it CAN fail, since ALLOWED is frozen and a check nothing can fail proves nothing. It found agent.bytes retained on its first run, which DES-13's inventory does not list — the collector no longer writes label lengths. A first version of the table listed approval.reviewer and approval.request as erasable SUB-KEYS and reported a correctly shredded record as retaining them: they are commitments whose VALUES are erasable, and the dead RESIDUE_ERASABLE_RETAINED code that mistake needed was removed The scan reports what it cannot read rather than skipping it: a chain line carrying a field inside unreadable JSON was invisible and the store was reported clean, while PRIV-05's claim is an exact residue.

title: Disclosure minimisation
statement: A disclosure reveals the named event and nothing else about other events' contents.
verify: Test asserts a disclosure pack contains exactly one salt and that no sibling leaf is reproducible from the pack
evidence: Exactly one salt, keyed by the disclosed record_seq, checked at BUILD time because a check on the recipient's side would run after the damage and a disclosure cannot be undone. The test states honestly what a Merkle path does reveal — the HASH of a sibling leaf, which is how an inclusion proof works — and asserts what it does not: no sibling leaf digest, no sibling salt, no sibling payload, so a sibling's content can be neither reproduced nor confirmed Adding the content salt closed one hole and could have opened a worse one, so a test asserts no SIBLING content salt appears: that would let a recipient confirm a guess at a payload nobody disclosed.

title: Disclose the tree-size leak
statement: Document that an inclusion proof reveals the log tree size, and that tree size is the count of ALL records — actions, heartbeats, policy events, gap declarations and padding — not a count of agent actions. The action count is therefore not directly disclosed, which is a weaker leak than an earlier draft claimed.
verify: Documentation review; a test asserts tree size exceeds the action count in any run containing heartbeats
evidence: The verifier reports records.by_kind beside tree_size, and a test asserts tree size exceeds the action count in a run holding heartbeats — with padding OFF, so it is not padding doing the work. `real` is named for not-padding rather than for actions, because heartbeats, gaps and policy events are real records and are not agent actions either, and conflating the two is the misreading PRIV-07 exists to prevent

title: Disclose the cadence leak

verify: Documentation review
evidence: docs/known-limits.md states the anchor-cadence leak: submitting checkpoints to a witness on a schedule tells that witness when the operator was busy. Published rather than reviewed — the DOC-05 test requires every uncovered attack and leak in that document to stay named

verify: Configuration test
evidence: Retention is a setting on the operator's own config applied to the operator's own storage by Store.applyRetention; nothing about it is a vendor policy and nothing about it is recorded in the chain, because a retention sweep is not an agent action
